t:
In the beginning there were two Gibberlings - Ase and Emla, and at the dawn of time, when Emla carried her first children under her heart, she put her hair into a braid. On the same night, babies were born, and the Threads of their Fates were connected to each other in a braid. Emla saw how strong this connection made the children, and henceforth she always put her long hair in many braids, and she and Ase had many sprouts, and they were all strong in their unity.

Each Gibberling in a sprout has its own Thread, and the Threads of the sprout are tightly intertwined. This makes the sprout strong, like a bunch of twigs that is harder to break than each twig individually. However, if one of the Threads of the sprout breaks, the other two also become weaker. Therefore, the families of our people always try to stick together and protect each other.

Woe to the family where a loner is born - this is a bad omen for the future Gibberling. Innumerable troubles will haunt them, their undertakings will be unsuccessful, they will be alone in this world, bringing grief to it, and only family care will save them from imminent death. That is why our people, despite settling around the world, always return to their roots - to Skalgard.

I'm sorry about those who threw your friend into the pit. They should have remembered who the Pridens were, even though we haven't seen them in a thousand years.

The Urun and Pridens are similar in many ways. The thing is, we were divided once - the Prides were led by the Voices, and the mad and cruel Urun were tyrants. Over the centuries of separation, they have become unlike each other! When Isa split, one of the most cruel renegade tribes, the white Urun Pridens, were trapped on the allod with us. Clashes between our peoples continued for centuries, and the Urun in their strength, cruelty and deceit surpassed even the Orcs of the past.

We are grateful to true Pridens. It was with their help that a great army was once created that drove the Orcs from Isa. Those Orcs were invaders who came from distant golden lands on ships. They tried to subjugate Isa for many centuries. But our great leaders - Thorri, Lok and Wald managed to unite the Gibberlings, Pridens, Heidruns, Zvergs and other peoples of Isa, and then finally defeated the Orcs.

And then the great Yok came - the sky rolled up like a scroll, the earth's crust cracked, and the waters of the oceans evaporated. The Great Void was advancing, and only the lands around the Ash Tree were untouched by it. At the time, many Gibberlings remained on Isa - but even more of them were outside it. Clans and families were separated...

We could only assume that if Isa survived thanks to the Ash Tree, then some other lands could have also remained intact. After all, human witch-doctors once took the seeds of Ash with them, and they sprouted in other parts.

But for a thousand years of loneliness on Isa, only three large clans survived. They sheltered the last representatives of the smaller clans. And the clans now carefully monitor the interweaving of the Threads of their bloodlines in order to prevent the degeneration of their people or the overpopulation on the island!

About a hundred and ten years ago, the spawn of the Void came - disgusting creatures who wanted to destroy the Ash! But hardened by centuries of battle with the Orcs, and then with the Urun, we managed to survive the Darkest Night and protect our allies. Many clans ceased to exist, but the demons also took many of the Urun. Our warriors managed to drive the remnants of their tribe into deep abandoned caves, the burrows of an ancient snake that once lived in the roots of the Ash Tree. There, in the darkness and hunger, they harbored anger for a long time and waited for their chance...

The Uruns... Some time ago they attacked us for the first time. Their army attacked Skalgard. They were led by a mighty leader, Kharyskhan...

The times of fierce battles returned to Isa, and blood again flowed on the snow under the shade of the Great Ash Tree, and the name of Kharyskhan was firmly woven into the Pattern on the annalistic carpet by the hands of the Thread Keepers. For this sinister leader of the Uruns constantly returned in a new guise. Every child knew his name.

But we found a solution - at the cost of huge losses, our heroes lured Kharyskhan into a trap and imprisoned his soul in a crystal of eternal ice. The crystal was hidden in a cave on the edge of our island, and the cave was sealed and disguised!

Our Elder is right. If you don't become a part of Isa, you won't achieve success. Everything in the world is interconnected — everyone has their own Thread of the Path. And the Threads of the Path are intertwined, forming the Fabric of the World. Tracking the events taking place in the world, and signs of changes in the Pattern of Fate, one can predict the location of the threads in the next rows of the Fabric of the World. Weave your Threads into our carpet and you will become a part of us.

Spiderweb will do, yes. But there is another task - find Finnie the Sharp-Sighted, I'm worried about him. He's on patrol - how is he doing?
Nice, nice. Well, I’ll get to work when the time comes. I’ll weave your fate into our carpet...
First, find Broddie and ask him how we can help the locals. That way we'll open their hearts to us.
Secondly, the Thread Keepers want to give you another task. They see that the inhabitants of Skalgard are frightened, and their Threads tremble. They know a way to set their minds at rest.

Thirdly, I see here a representative of a people we've never seen before - they are called the Heidruns. Her name is Hadne, I saw her running after baby Gibberlings. Talk to her. We could use such friends.

Fourthly, I feel something strange in the Thread of this Gerda. And the meteorite amulet that belongs to her is very unusual. There's nowhere it could have come from! The Sharps might know where this meteorite trinket came from!

No, I haven't seen the tree maiden from the other world. Since Ratatoskr says we were scattered during the teleportation, maybe she wound up in some other region on Isa... I will keep an ear out - if I learn anything, I'll let you know.
Sometimes you fall into your dreams and find something you don't expect...
Alright, ready your weapon! Let's see how you fare against me!
I don't know if I want to punch someone... or have a drink...
And it's not three of us against you! We only have one bow!
Hadne!! It's not fair to ask for help! It doesn't count!!
It does, too! Alright, I'll go to Hadne...
You didn't find me! I can't see you, so you can't see me! Pfft!
Next time no one will find me!
How would you look after me? I'd rather go back to Hadne!
Who are you? I don't know you. Hadne!! Hadne!!

What a weird blue gleam! No, buddy. This is the first time I've seen a metal like this. You say it's the pendant of a local villager? I don't even know what to think. I don't think it's from these parts, but you say it's been here for a long time... hmm...

The metal has its own song. And you need to be able to hear it...

Can you, Orcs, hear the song of metal?Do you, Pridens, have your own blacksmiths? They say you used to...They say other peoples know the way to the heart of metal. Do you know it?They say other peoples know the way to the heart of metal. Do you know it?They say other peoples know the way to the heart of metal. Do you know it?They say other peoples know the way to the heart of metal. Do you know it?They say other peoples know the way to the heart of metal. Do you know it?Other Gibberlings, can you hear this song?
No, I have never seen anything like it. A very unusual metal, but I'm sure I've never come across anything like it. And I've collected a lot of ore here on Isa.
What could be better than the sound of a hammer?
I have never come across items made of metal that would look like this pendant! And I have seen a lot of swords, chainmail and helmets in my life. Not to mention pokers and pitchforks...
Fire and metal are what blacksmiths work with. Our blades serve Skalgard!
Perhaps we have some relatives here? It's possible. All our ancestors lived on Isa once! Oh, to find relatives...
Isa! An incredibly beautiful island! And we found it!
My brother and I have been dreaming of finding relatives for a long time! So we think maybe there are some distant relatives among the local clans? I wonder if there's a way to find out...
We are on Isa? I still can't believe it!

"In our villages

We have these maidens.

Amorous for a day only,

And then - nothing,"

Lok said jokingly.

The brothers nodded:

"This is no good!

We need a sure way!"

Ilko thought for a while,

Then said,

"If you don't wish to wait

For the Star of Fortune...

There are other sagas

Which sing about marvels

About the one who created

All the living things.

He rarely appeared,

But whoever saw him knows:

Num is the creator of the living.

He must be wiser than all of us."

"That's right, Ilko,

Since he is the father to all of us,

He must know for real,

How to escape fate.

How do we find

Num who is invisible?

If he has a house,

Maybe that's where he is?"

Wise Ilko said,

"Num's house is unknown.

But there are signs

That can show the way.

When you see a Rainbow,

He is at the edge

Farthest from you.

Look there.

Where the sky shines,

From horizon to horizon,

Num will be close,

You can find him.

Where the winds were born

And the fires of volcanoes,

There are traces of creation,

And Num's abode.

But those brave ones

Who do not believe in fate

And who want to fight it

Should remember this:

By challenging the might

That is stronger than gods,

Brave madmen

Will bring doom."

"We will not be stopped

By threats of Fate,

A warrior does not fear

Empty words,"

So saying,

The warriors left.

The path took them far away,

To a place full of signs.

The north received the brothers,

Where the radiance of the sky

Illuminates the earth

But does not warm it.

The path is long and difficult,

The journey took many days.

There is nothing but ice and rocks,

And spoils are scarce.

Every day is shorter

Under the dim sun,

The night grows boundlessly,

Darkness brings cold.

One night a storm

Wakes up the brothers.

A veil of snow

Covers everything around them.

They see through the snowstorm

That someone is approaching -

A silhouette

With a shaky gait.

Once the fire dispelled

The darkness that hid the image,

The brothers were horrified:

It was a frozen corpse!

Features and clan marks were hidden

Under the iron mask.

His armor was covered

With hoarfrost patterns.

Thorri swung his hammer

At the evil spirit!

But suddenly the uninvited guest

Said quietly,

"Who are you and why are you here?"

The brothers were surprised.

"We are Gibberlings

Looking for the house of Num."

Like you, I once searched

For the House of the Creator...

The road was not easy,

I fell, killed by Frost."

"We do not fear Frost!"

Thorri answered.

"It is worth fearing

the Evil God of Cold.

Here he reigns supreme,

Eradicating life.

The deadly frost

Kills outright.

Be afraid to meet

The ice maiden here.

If you look even once

Into the eyes of an Isfrun,

You will turn to ice,

And your life force will fade.

Even the Junes fear

The powers of the harsh ice.

There are many other

Creatures of nightmare here.

Ice worms,

Jotunns and Wargs...

If you go further,

It will be even more dangerous.

Icy expanses

Are not for the living!"

"We will reach our goal,"

Said the brothers.

"The Threads of our Fate

have become stronger!

Thank you for your advice...

What is your name?"

The dead one answered them:

They used to call me Nagle."

As the storm subsided,

They said goodbye to the guest,

And set out.

Many days passed.

Thorri often lifted

The hammer when necessary.

Many different creatures,

Some of them nameless,

He struck down with a blow,

Powerful and brave.

Lok scouted out the land.

With his cunning tricks,

He sneaked into the dwellings

of snow giants.

After stealing food,

He returned to his brothers.

Wald, full of advice,

Knew the habits of monsters

And taught his brothers

How to avoid them.

Thus they reached the sea.

The end of their journey was close.

Massive mountains nearby

Were the borders of this world.

There, in the distance,

Burned a flame brighter than the sun.

It was their destination,

The end of distant wanderings.

The brothers found there

 A wonderful old man

With a white beard,

Wearing scarlet clothes.

"Are you called Num?"

Lok asked fearlessly.

"Teach us, old one,

How to avoid Fate!"

"Foolish children!"

Num answered angrily.

"In vain

you came to my halls!

I do know of a way

To avoid fate.

But it is infeasible

For the Sparks of mortals!

To argue with fate,

You must be free

Of all the chains

And fetters of the world.

But you are held tightly

By the Thread of Fate,

A vigilant Weaver

Spun it before your birth."

The brothers listened,

And in heavy thoughts

Set out for home.

Their families were waiting.

The threshold is in sight.

Within reach...

But wait, listen -

Bells are ringing!

This means the Orcs

Attacked viciously again.

The brothers did not wait -

Rushed to help!

A hard-won victory -

The brothers survived

Miraculously in this battle.

Such is the will of Fate!

Accepting the Threads,

The Gibberling brothers

Resigned themselves

To their great fate.

Future alliances

Needed a base

They were destined to build.

Votin gave Thorri

His mighty troops,

Lok will appease the Zvergs.

Wald will think of a way

To approach the harsh Pridens.

Great-grandchildren will continue

Their Threads in the Pattern.

What is meant to be will happen!

The Orcs will be gone from Isa!

Sagas will remember

Thorri, Lok, and Wald!

The glory of the Gibberlings

Is preserved for centuries!

Evil storms raged,

White snow fell,

The house stood strong,

Steady and unshakeable.

He who was the oldest

Among the harsh leaders,

Became a father for the first time -

To three brothers.

Thorri was the first,

Lok was next,

Wald came last,

Votin was their father.

Three Gibberlings -

Their sprout was strong!

It was noisy in the house,

Fun every day!

The children were growing up,

Year after year.

Thorri boasted of his strength,

Lok was the most cunning of all.

Wald loved to listen,

Sitting next to his father:

What others say,

Who believes what.

Who brings news

To their home.

At this time,

News was the same:

Hordes of evil Orcs,

Who came uninvited,

Besieged again

the Gibberling lands.

They burn, break, destroy,

Everything that can be touched.

They are getting close

To the Ash Tree.

The Gibberlings seek

Salvation in the sea.

Votin with his troops

Defends the Great Tree.
This rune-covered menhir contains part of an ancient saga...

This rune-covered menhir contains part of an ancient saga...

But first you need to hear the previous part.

The years went by

Quickly for the brothers,

And their father's troops

Grew bigger and stronger.

The time came for vengeance

On the Orc people!

The old Votin

Sent the sons to battle.

Thorri chose a hammer

Forged by the Zvergs

And left his father's house

Without saying a word.

Lok said goodbye

To his mother and father,

To his uncles and aunt,

And other relatives.

Wald said a few things

At the threshold of the house.

He promised to return

Once the Orcs were defeated.

The three brothers left,

Watched by sharp eyes.

And words followed them,

Full of spells.

It was a maiden

Of a different kind.

She was called black,

Her fur darker than soot.

Her name was Seida.

Braiding threads

In wonderful patterns,

She saw clearly

Signs and omens

In the Fabric of the Universe.

Regarding the fate of the three brothers

Seida was silent.

Numerous Orcs

Were slain by Thorri's hammer.

Many were scared into fleeing

Straight into Lok's traps.

Then came an avalanche

Of iron shields.

The hird's weapons clanged,

Sharp spears gleamed.

Scarlet flowers

bloomed on Isa's snow.

The Gibberlings' fury

Spared no Orc.

And the enemies fled

In a terrible panic.

It is true that in unity

Was the Gibberlings' strength!

"It's time to go home!"

Thorri told the brothers.

There were spoils:

Silver, gold,

Wonderful armor,

marvelous weapons!

They would have something to show

To Votin and the others!

The journey home was long

The brothers whiled it away

In conversation.

Lok said, thoughtful:

"And where, brothers,

Did these Orcs come from?

Old man told us

They didn't exist!"

"They say the Orcs once lived

In the warm lands of the south

Far away from here.

But they went overseas -

Humans drove them out.

And also dragons,"

Said Wald

who knew the sagas.

"What are Humans?"

Lok asked.

"Humans are Humans,
We have not met them.

But the Orcs know

That somewhere in the south,

Where there is enough land,

There are plenty of them.

There would be even more of them,

If not for the dragons

That burn down

Everything they see.

The dragons feel hatred

For all the living.

The Orc nomads' camps

Died in flames.

After leaving the steppes,

And building boats,

The Orcs moved straight

to Isa as a horde."

The brothers were quiet

For the next part of the journey.

They thought about Orcs,

Humans, and dragons.

The home was now

Only one day away.

Thorri said to Lok

One night in camp,

"I wish we could go back,

Drive the Orcs back to the Humans.

Save our home

From this endless threat.

"That’s right, brother!"

Lok nodded, thinking,

"It’s a pity we are few in number,

And we have no dragons!

I wish we could get

More weapons

From the wise Heidruns,

Praidens, or Zvergs."

They kept going,

Talking all the while

about upcoming battles.

Look - we are home!

In celebration of another victory,

A feast was held.

Brothers were honored,

With raised cups.

Many Gibberlings

Drank beer there,

Ate fish

And a lot of cheese.

And tales were told,

Each better than the last,

Around the mead hall

Deep into the night.

In the morning, early,

When it's dark,

And the fog is still

Over the water,

Three brothers left the house

And went to the square.

They saw a maiden there,

Black as midnight.

"Glorious is your path, brothers!"

That was Seida's voice.

"I ask you to hear

What the Threads promise us."

"Tell me, sister,"

Lok intervened quickly.

"Will we be rid of the Orcs?

Will we drive them out completely?"

Seida answered,

"Sagas will sing about you,

They will carry your feat

Through the centuries to your descendants.

But I see dangers

That threaten the whole of Isa.

Horrible fate awaits us!

The power of insidious Fate!

The Threads of the universe

Tell me this:

Soon the world will plunge

Into the void of oblivion!

The roots of the world will crack,

Rocks will fall into the abyss,

And sea waters

Will boil all at once.

The wolf will swallow the sun,

And the stars will die out.

Darkness will swallow Isa,

devouring everything.

Many souls will die,

Many words will be forgotten,

And the people of Isa

Will perish in the pitch darkness!

That moment is called 'Yok',"

So said Seida.

The brothers fell silent,

Horrified…

"But there are sprouts of hope

Amidst the nightmare,

Seida said again,

"Isa will survive!

A new world will arise

From the wreckage of the old ones,

Great-grandfather, Prophetic Ash Tree

Will be our salvation.

But Fate is treacherous!

Centuries later

Trouble will come again,

Darkness will cover the whole world.

I see it so clearly:

The tree is dying,

The ancient enemy has been awakened,

There is no rest for the dead!

Deadly Frost will come,

And countless enemies

Whose skin is white.

I see it through time.

Blood ties get stronger:

Pilgrim's children

Will take ragged weaving

And tie it into a whole.

And the flower of hope

Will bloom at the Tree,

The news will rush further

To the wonderful land of stars.

This is just the beginning.

I see an ominous city,

It is full of the dead,

Summoned against their will.

Light and darkness in battle

Argue with each other,

But in vain:

Their fate is inevitable.

A new god will rise -

He who took the power

From the unfortunate sisters

Who forgot the law:

What Fate decides

Will happen.

There is no power in the world,

That would change that."

The maiden Seida's

Speeches have faded.

The Gibberling brothers

conferred for a long time.

"You won't scare us!"

Thorri said,

"While my hammer is in my hand,

I will not accept this fate!"

If the pattern is known,

And not yet woven...

We must take the Threads into our hands

And fool Fate!"

So said Lok,

The cunning trickster.

Wald, after much thought,

Supported the idea.

"Since Seida does not know

How to avoid fate,

We will seek advice

from other peoples."

So it was decided,

And there was no reason to delay.

On the same day, the three brothers

Set off on another journey.

The path took them far away,

To the foot of Muspel

Where good Heidruns

settled among the grass.

The Gibberlings were greeted

By Ilko, the chief of the horned ones.

The people welcomed the guests,

Offering mead.

"Tell us, wise one,

How to argue with Destiny?

How to avoid Fate,

What do the Threads say?"

The Heidrun chief said,

"Yes, Fate is harsh.

What it decided to weave

Will surely happen.

We gave this evil force

A different name.

We call it the Weaver

That spins Threads.

But we believe

That another power exists.

It gives a chance

to those it favors.

If Luck loves

Her chosen one,

They will avoid Fate

And deceive the Threads.

But while she falls in love quickly,

She falls out of it just as easily.

The circle will come around again,

And luck will pass.
Great, now we can rest easy!
Great, now we can rest easy!

We have many legends... I could tell you all of them, but it will take a few days! But believe me, they are worth hearing, because they tell about the most courageous warriors who battle giant monsters or hordes of wild Urun! And our warriors beat them all! They scatter them easily with one - or rather, with three left paws!

And our elders select the most cunning and strong Stalwarts who will win the tournament or accomplish a great feat of arms. We Stalwarts love to match our strength against other people's, and we usually resolve our disputes is the arena which you have already seen! We don't fight to the death, of course, just to the first cries of "Ah! Leave me alone!"

And we don't divide people into boys and girls - even the cutest member of the clan can easily beat up a mountain cat.

Members of the Heidrun family are of great help to us. They help with the equipment: they have the strength to hammer the pieces of red hot iron into shape. In this they are as good as the Zvergs who, alas, are long gone.

And of course, our clan pays great attention to signs related to luck in battle. What weapon should we choose? How to weave wool so it protects from a strong blow?

A Stalwart should know all this!

Here, listen: The first note is dated January 13, 765 from Yok

Some notes are missing - apparently Koll left the ones he considered important. This is what he wrote:

«We leave the island which belongs to the elves of the Grandeur clan and continue our search.

The discovery has caused dismay in our ranks - many of the other captains, like Eric, believe that we need to form a temporary alliance with these people and take advantage of their hospitality for a while - until we find Isa.

But I have doubts - there are few of us, and judging by what we have learned, there are many of those outlanders. Can we remain free? Or will we be forced to reveal our secret? Will we become soldiers of foreign wars?

We can always come back later. In the meantime, we'll keep going and see where the currents in the Great Nothing take us.»

"I couldn't believe my ears when the crew told me they saw an island with a huge tree ahead. Is it Isa? The Astral can be deceptive - it shows mirages and false visions, so you can't trust your eyes. But we won't get another opportunity - we are heading for this land.

On our home island many believed that Isa had survived. If they were right, then we would be the first to set foot on the lands of Isa after Yok.

Of course, the matter of our agreement with Brus remains. I intend to fulfill it. After all, without Vegvisir I wouldn't have been able to find the way. The Orcs are not a threat now. Without their Great Mage, they will not be able to create a new Horde. Even with a commander like Skulnar the Northwind."

We've been wrecked. It's not easy to moor when the astral winds turn into a real storm. At the last moment, we were thrown onto one of the local mountains. Now the Freya, it seems, is forever chained to this peak.

Unfortunately, we lost a few people. It's also terribly cold here in the mountains. We can no longer stay here. We should try to find the Gibberlings that should still be on Isa. Before we fell, I think I saw a city.

I'm sure the local Gibberlings will help us, so we need to get out even if it's difficult.

Well, we managed to reach the city - Skalgard, one of the few settlements that still remain on Isa. My people managed to survive Yok, albeit at great cost. I met the legendary Thread Keepers or, putting it simply, the Spinners. We talked for a long time while I recounted everything I knew. I told them how our small settlement survived in the midst of the Great Nothing, how Sven discovered a way to travel in the Astral, how we found other peoples.

The Thread Keepers, thanks to what they learned from me and with the help of the Ash Tree, looked into the darkness of the past. But also into the darkness of the future, knowing what will happen now that I have found Isa. They promised to think and give an answer the next day.

The Thread Keepers told me what they saw in the future. According to the prophecy, Isa would have been discovered and drawn into the war between the League and the Empire. In the fight for the power of the Ash Tree, the two great states would destroy it, thereby dooming the remnant of Isa sustained by the Great Tree.

In addition, the return of Skulnar also promises great trouble. The Spinners say that when the Orc chief returns to the Horde, he will be able to get a Great Mage to serve him. Together, Skulnar and the Great Mage will start a new Great Feast. In the end, they will conquer the whole world, enslaving the rest of the free peoples. Such is the Orcs' destiny if Skulnar returns.

I took time to think. I have a difficult decision to make.

I renounced my oath to the old shaman. Instead, I decided to help the Thread Keepers imprison the malevolent soul of Skulnar - time after time, this Orc leader returns in the guise of the Urun - one of the subspecies of the Priden people. He did much harm to my people, so even a broken oath does not weigh on my conscience that much.

Together, we decided to use my Vegvisir to reach Skulnar's soul through the blood connection and ensnare it.

This ritual is extremely dangerous. I don't know if we can survive it. But this is the least I can do for the Gibberlings on Isa, since my arrival has brought with it the threat the Thread Keepers speak of.

We were successful - with my help, the Thread Keepers were able to capture the spirit of Skulnar. Now he is imprisoned in an ice cave on the coast of the island. If Fate wills it, he will remain there forever. Vegvisir has been destroyed, so no one else will be able to find Isa... At least I hope so.

However, the Thread Keepers say that I am the problem now. Other Gibberlings have seen me - and they ask questions, expecting an explanation. They want to know who I am and where I came from. But knowledge of the outside world may encourage them to look for ways to get off Isa. Such temptation will not be tolerated!

The Thread Keepers say there is a better way to keep Isa safe. To do this, they need to break all the Threads that could lead someone from the outside world to Isa. Including those Threads that connect me to my brother and his offspring. Most likely, this will kill me, but there seems to be no other way. Isa is too important to lose.

Despite the broken Threads that connected me to my family and brother, I survived - albeit almost miraculously. I have never felt so sad and lonely. But this sacrifice is necessary for the sake of Isa. Now everyone will think that I died without achieving my goal. But I'm warmed by the knowledge that I did it. I have lived a long life, I have seen a lot, so I'm glad I will end my days here, in the homeland of my people.

At the urging of the Thread Keeper, I leave Skalgard. I will go far from the inhabited lands to where only the Werebears and the remaining Urun live. No one will know where the nameless exile came from, but my appearance will not raise questions.

I settled in this cave, and although I'm capable of procuring supplies for myself, life is still very harsh here. It's extremely cold, and on top of everything else it's hard to be alone when there is no one to talk to.

I need to learn how to communicate with the local Zvergs who, apparently, are already used to me and treat me as a familiar part of the environment. If I can establish regular contact with them, then it will be much easier for me - I can exchange what I have for what they have.

Very interesting. I thought I would never meet another Gibberling again, and yet such a meeting took place. One of the brave huntresses who had been chasing a beast day and night came across my shelter. Her name is Frigga, and I think it's a funny coincidence.

Frigga is incredibly brave: Isa is too crowded for her, so she wants to explore all of it. I didn't tell her my whole story, but she is still interested in how I survive here in the wilderness. I gave her some of my supplies. She has gone back to Skalgard, but it looks like she might return. This makes sense - prey is abundant in the local wilderness.

Unbelievable! The Orcs, our old enemies, also survived. And we met them here, on the Izune allod. As far as I understand, the Orcs were in the same position - except for the fact that Izune was their homeland, and so they did not need to look for it. But like us, they are just pieces on someone else's chessboard. Some time ago, their ruler, the supreme shaman Rodogor, made a deal with the Empire that guaranteed the survival of their race in alliance with a human nation, the Xadaganians. Perhaps such a fate awaits us? I'd rather it did not.

The Orcs are hostile. They seem to think we're some type of goblins, so they're trying to enslave us. We need to gather supplies before we move on, but I'm afraid it won't be easy.

Frigga decided to stay with me. We have seen each other many times, and each time she comes, she spends more and more time with me. She says it must be fate, and I don’t feel like arguing. Perhaps she is right.

Life here is hard, of course, but now it will be easier. The experienced huntress is not afraid of difficulties.

And one more thing - Frigga says she is with children. This is good news.

We have a daughter. One, not three. This is rather unusual for us Gibberlings, and as a rule, the birth of just one portends misfortune. Perhaps it's true. Nevertheless, I'm very happy. So is Frigga.

She suggests that it was probably a consequence of the Thread Keepers' ritual that severed the connection between me and my family. Which is a pity. I would have preferred this sacrifice to be only mine, not my entire family's. But what can we do now? We can love her the way she is.

We've made a tough decision. Driva must grow up surrounded by her kindred. The way Frigga and I grew up. It won't be easy for her to be alone, and it's another reason not to deprive her of other Gibberlings' company. Therefore, we will take her to Skalgard. She'll be safe there, and that's all that matters.

But I would like to give her something to remember us by. I asked Brock, one of my Zverg friends, to make an amulet for her. I took a bit of the meteorite that held my ship in the astral plane. I hope it will become a family heirloom that will be passed down through generations of my descendants. It's the least I could do.

Frigga took Driva to Skalgard and gave her to the Thread Keepers. They set a condition... However, I won't say what it is. Perhaps someday later, I will write about it, but now I'm too disturbed and upset. Someday I will make sense of everything and write it all down in detail. But not right now.

Frigga and I are sad, but we are still happy for our daughter. What matters is she's happy. Everything else is unimportant.

There is something I have wanted to talk about for a long time. The secret I have been silent about for many years now burns me from the inside. I no longer want to keep it. By entrusting it to paper, hopefully I will make this burden lighter.

If the Thread of my kind here is connected to the Thread of my brother's family in the outside world, Isa can be returned to that world. Without this, any search for it in the astral plane will be fruitless. Whoever searches for it will find nothing.

But if the two Threads are reconnected, our descendants will once again be bound by the ancient oath that calls for the return of the Orc leader. And the return of Isa means he will be freed. And then the prophecy about the Horde that will conquer the whole world will be fulfilled.

I have very little strength left. This is probably my last entry in the journal. Everything comes to an end, and the Thread of my Fate must also be broken. I will go on an eternal journey. But although my path was not the easiest, I leave with hope. The Thread of my family will continue with Driva and her descendants. Sooner or later it will return to the predetermined pattern.

There! Koll is a real hero, of course! We'll make sure everyone knows what he did!

We've been in captivity for almost a month now. Is this our Fate? Eric says we should stay on the allod of the Grandeur clan, Glock suggests waiting for the Xadaganians and trying to negotiate with them by revealing the secret of our ships to them. But I'm afraid they'll figure it out anyway when they search the ship.

The Orcs are crude animals. They treat goblins like slaves, and it looks like we will be treated the same way. I'm glad they were banished from Isa at some point. They say that Brus, the current supreme shaman and Rodogor's son, comes from the Northwind clan, the one we defeated on Isa.

Brus is acting strangely. He forbade the Orcs from boarding our ship. He is waiting for something - but what? The Xadaganians? Maybe. They say the Empire has its ways of loosening tongues.

Something incredible happened today. I finally met this Brus. He is smarter than he looks. Certainly smarter than his henchmen. Brus demanded that I come alone, and we had a long discussion. Nobody needs to know what he told me. I will write it down in my journal for now.

Brus wants us to find their ancient leader. For some reason, he believes he is somehow alive. Skulnar the Northwind, the Bane of Humans - after the Orcs were expelled from Isa, his clan led the Orc people and tried to conquer the world. Skulnar was killed, but his body was retrieved and sent to Isa!

Brus offers a deal. A magic oath. He will let us go, and I will find Skulnar. And Isa. I'm not sure. I don't know what to do.

Failure again! The Kanians are after the secret of our ships! Nobody can be trusted. Eric says we should negotiate - we can demand land from Kania in exchange for the secret, and Glock thinks that Xadagan can offer us more.

But they don't understand: we must find our homeland, Isa!

Nobody knows there's a way to find it. What Brus gave me is still with me. If I fulfill my oath, then we can find our homeland.

I spoke to my brothers. Now they know my secret, too. But they don't want me to keep my promise to the Orc.

I don't know what to do.

For many years now we have been wandering between allods, from one to another, and we can't stop anywhere. Brus is long dead, but this oath weighs on me. Alas, there is no way to find Isa - to search for it, we'd need considerable supplies which we don't have.

Right now no one can promise that this attempt will not fail. We need to be better prepared.

Until now, only my brothers and I have known about our agreement with Brus. They will not reveal the secret, and I... I'm not ready to share that just yet.

A lot of time has passed since we left our island. Over the years we have discovered allods unknown to us and new peoples that we have not seen for hundreds of years.

We face a fateful decision: the Gibberlings don't have the numbers to survive alone in this new world, but we can't stay on our tiny island either. We need a new home.

The Elves have been of great help to us, although I know that they expect to get the secret of astral travel for it. Albert de Grandeur promises that the Emperor of Kania will give us one of the allods - Ingos which is in many ways similar to Isa.

Now my people are arguing - whether we should accept the offer or continue to look for Isa.

The answer has to be given soon.

I told them about Brus, leaving out the details. Few people believe the promises of the Orcs, but it seems that we have no other choice. Either we will make one last attempt to find Isa, or we will be forced to make an agreement with Kania.

They decided to give me time until the end of the year. By then, I must find Isa. If this does not happen, they will be free to make any decision.

Only one of my brothers is still alive. He stayed with his family, and I promised him that soon I would return with good news.

The team I have assembled is made up of the most determined, courageous, and foolhardy sailors. We'll either find Isa or die trying!

We have been sailing through the Astral for many months now. The Elven writings they kindly shared with us proved very useful. True, none of them had been where we are right now - the Astral destroys everything it touches. If it weren't for the secret that Sven had discovered, our ship would have melted like a burning candle.

The Astral is empty - we didn't name it the Great Nothing for nothing. There is nothing here but eternal radiance, flashes of lights that can drive you crazy, and lightning bolts on the horizon. We float at the will of astral currents and winds - there are no other ways to move here. Oars can't do anything.

Thankfully, over the years we have learned to navigate it. The winds here work almost the same as in the open sea which no longer exists. And the magic device that Albert de Grander gave me allows me to trace the contours of the map.

Brus promised that my runic magic compass - a Vegvisir sprinkled with his blood - would lead me to his distant relative, Skulnar, and Isa. In return, I had to hand over the Vegvisir with the blood to the leader himself. If Rodogor's and Brus's theory is correct, this magic of theirs will help establish a connection between Skulnar and his descendants, and then bring the leader of the Northwind clan into the outside world.

Alas, it looks like the Orc made a mistake somewhere. We were running out of time. If we don't find Isa in the next few days, we'll have to turn back home.

Hello, hello, we are here on behalf of the Historians. We are interested in Koll's journal! Well, it's an extremely important historical document... We can't afford to lose it! Fortunately, they didn’t use it for kindling, so we asked Gerda to let us make a copy... If you haven't read it yet, we can tell you what's in there...

Ho-ho-ho! Hey, sea cadet! Our clan is the most glorious clan on Isa. Why? We are the last clan that is truly faithful to the vanished sea. That's why we settled here, on the coast. Even if the Empty Sea is not like the oceans of old, there is still enough fish here, so we can build our little boats and feed all of Isa!

But the Fishermen clan is not just about sitting for hours over the ice-hole! Among the members of our clan, the competition for the biggest catch never ceases, and our regular fishing trips are like little campaigns: we carefully prepare the ship, crew, stocks of bait, and durable equipment for the largest inhabitants of the icy sea.

The coming weather, bite, and the best bait are determined by a variety of signs. To say nothing of the importance of the ship's name!

We have all sorts of legends! Most often they tell about the chilling dangers of the merciless sea and about daredevils who overcome all obstacles and return with an incredible catch.

Lyngbakr is just one of those legends! A huge bloodthirsty fish capable of overturning a boat has devoured many unfortunate hunters. The current Elder of the clan is Styr Ruff: usually the captains of the most successful fishing vessels become Elders. He and his sister Helga lost their brother to this monster's jaws and vowed to take revenge sooner or later.

But we also have stories about other monsters - Morgens, Kelpies, Skrimslas, Klippdasses, Merrows, Sjoras, Hafgufas, and even Krakens! Someone sees them from time to time, although usually we find only herring in the nets!

In addition to many stories about successful fishing trips, our clan also carefully preserves ancient legends about distant sea journeys since the time before the cataclysm. A reminder of these times is right in front of you: the remains of ancient ships encased in ice, still lying among the coastal rocks.

Fish is not just food! It's also a way of life. Our arrows are made of fish bones, we use fish oil, our clothes and jewelry are decorated with scales, and you'll have an opportunity to try all kinds of fish dishes. Don't forget the huge fish skeleton on the roof of the house!

Hey, don't just stand there. Buy something! We have all sorts of goods since we travel all over Isa and barter with others... Still, we prefer hard currency. If you don't have any Skalgard coin right now, we'll take gold, too!

Yo-ho-ho! The Meadmakers are the most peaceful and cheerful clan who lives side by side with the Heidruns here, on the edge of the warm Mead Valley. And believe me - you will not find such experts in strong drinks anywhere else on Isa! We keep coming up with new recipes and test them ourselves or with our neighbors. It's no wonder that we are the only suppliers of the best mead for feasts in Skalgard.

And here we regularly arrange competitions to see who outdrinks the rest, and that's also how we elect our Elder. Yes! Skol! Every important completed task should be celebrated! That's our tradition...

Our clan keeps the secret of special strong mead which has a powerful warming effect and grants incredible courage. This ancient recipe is passed strictly from one Elder to another. It's made with various meadow herbs and berries, honey of giant bees, and some secret ingredient that I can’t tell you about... Well, unless you win the trust of the Guardian Surt, and he tells you himself.

We don't just drink mead. Some of our recipes can be used to make powerful combustibles. A barrel of that brew can go off with quite a bang!

We also have stories. And no wonder. One only has to down a cup of mead, then go out for a walk in the Valley - something will definitely happen. You might run into a Clurichaun. Or a Jotunn! And apparently you can beat up a Jotunn easily when you're drunk! At least that's what the men keep saying. So don't be surprised if you hear something like that!

As for our beliefs, predictions and omens are often used to determine the right time for gathering herbs and brewing mead. Though most of our signs promise booze in the near future. And due to regular libations, our clan’s Carpet of Fate is a bit uneven…
Hic! The mead is good today!
Each Thread has a set length.

Once upon a time we weaved the Pattern, but now we make sure the Threads do not break prematurely.

Should the need arise, we will tie a knot!
What would you like to know?

Everything in our settlement is run by the Elder, the most respected Gibberling of their clan. There is a council where the heads of all the clans and other respected Gibberlings decide on issues that affect all of our people.

A Chief Elder can be chosen among the Elders - they are responsible for military affairs and other events, so usually it's the Elder of the Stalwart clan. Once upon a time, it was the Chief Elders who made agreements with the Heidruns, Pridens and Zvergs, but now we only do business with the Heidruns whose leader usually lives in the Meadmakers' village. We do not have dealings with the Urun - we only fight them.

The decision of the Elders is the law, and they are rarely challenged. All in all, the community is a big team that shares sorrows and joys. A clan is a large family where several different generations exist together, connected by intricate family threads...

We value family above all else, and the worst crime is a crime against our clan and especially our sprout. The capital punishment is exile and renunciation.

The exile, or "skogarmaor", is deprived of all rights, separated from the sprout, and forced to survive alone in the frosty lands! Their thread in the tribe's Carpet of Fate is cut off, and the criminal is "dead" for the community. The sprout has the option to go into exile with them.

We do not believe in immortality and therefore place high value on life. If fate favors the traitor, they will be able to survive even in harsh conditions, and then the council of clans, perhaps, will consider the option of pardoning them.

A less severe punishment is the Judgment of Fate, a difficult test that the offender must pass. For example, defeat a powerful monster that lives in the lands of deadly frost and come back alive. Few people manage that, but if Fate favors them, they will be exonerated!

Strong family ties are the most important thing for the Gibberlings. What does the word "ties" mean? It's a “knot” that binds the Threads of the family together.

Our people are very fertile: the birth of only twins is a cause for grief for parents, but triplets are the norm. For three brothers or sisters there is a name: a sprout. Members of the same sprout perfectly understand each other and very rarely can live separately: life is very boring without relatives. Moreover, there are cases when the death of one Gibberling is soon followed by the death of their brothers or sisters!

When Gibberlings embark on dangerous adventures, they go together - all three of them, the whole sprout. A lone Gibberling is a rarity in our world.

Why do we call triplets a "sprout"? It's because of the legend of the Great Ash Tree and the fact that Ase and Emla were created from its branches! Hence the "sprout"!

The Thread Keepers say that at the dawn of time, when Emla carried her first children under her heart, she put her hair into a braid. On the same night, babies were born, and the Threads of their Fates were connected to each other in a braid. Emla saw how strong this connection made the children, and henceforth she always put her long hair in many braids, and she and Ase had many sprouts, and they were all strong in their unity.

From that came the unique feature of our people. Each Gibberling in a sprout has their own Thread, and the Threads of the sprout are tightly intertwined. This makes the sprout strong, like a bunch of twigs that is harder to break than each twig individually. However, if one of the Threads of the sprout breaks, the other two also become weaker. Therefore, the families of our people always try to stick together and protect each other. The birth of a lone Gibberling places on them the stigma of a "bringer of bad luck", and while measures are taken to provide care and protection for them, they are considered weak and "lost".

The idea of interwoven Threads is also reflected in the community's Carpet of Fate. On the birthday of a sprout, the community's Thread Keepers measure out threads for them, which are then woven into one and then used in the overall Pattern. They try to measure out a great length of thread to ensure a long life for the sprout.

And the tradition of braiding hair into many braids is still widespread among the Gibberlings of both sexes. It is also believed that Emla's ability to influence the weaving of the Threads of her descendants makes her the first Weaver in history!
Oh, it's so hard to rhyme! You have to count the syllables!

As you already know, we do not welcome immortality and do not believe in the Light that you told us about. We believe that, in the natural order of things, each Thread is spun, then woven into the Pattern, then cut.

Yes, occasional cases of resurrection are present in ancient legends, and we interpret them as exceptional events, when the Thread was so important for the Pattern that it could not have been broken, and the spirit of Emla herself tied and wove the broken Thread back in. The same can be accomplished by the mystical powers of a Weaver. Unn claims that you are a Weaver, but it still needs to be proven! She could be wrong...

It is customary to burn the dead. Cut off from the common carpet by the clan's Thread Keepers, the remainder of their unused thread is put into the palms of the deceased. Before Yok, it was customary to scatter the ashes over the sea, and especially revered representatives of the people were sent on their last voyage in a small boat which was set on fire by a shot from a distance.

Now no one wants to send the ashes of their dead to the unknown and frightening abyss of Ginnungagap! This is how the Stone Boats appeared - the outlines of the ships that you see here laid out on the ground with rocks. Inside the boat, the ashes of members of the same clan are buried, and their names are written on the stones that form the sides. This is how the old forgotten tradition of the "family ship" is preserved, and the deceased get the opportunity to go with their family on a happy "endless journey".

Over time, there were more and more stones, more and more decks were added to the boats, and now the boats of the oldest families resemble many-storied pyramids, on top of which the stones of the first of their kind rest. It is said that occasionally you can meet the Gibberlings who come to visit their ancestors, and sometimes you see "echoes of fate" in the form of barely noticeable ghosts lost in the fog.

Yes, Stone boats are laid out near the Ash which symbolizes the return of travelers to their progenitor. This place is called the Harbor of Eternal Wanderers...

The history of our people is stored primarily in long Carpets of Fate which reflect the interweaving of the clan members' destinies. But knowing how to read the carpet is not enough - you need to do it beautifully! The art of composing sagas and songs based on events woven in carpets is mastered by skalds. The most famous of skalds is Snorri who composed the story of three brothers who drove the Orcs from Isa.

To honor the events of the past, our people have erected runestones at the sites of these events. Even now you can find these ancient boulders and read about the most important episodes in the history of Isa.

There has always been a place on Isa that is sacred to all the Gibberlings. A place at the junction of the realms of ice and fire, where the Great Tree grows. From its branches of which, according to legend, the first Gibberlings were created: Ase and Emla.

The Ash is a powerful place of power which greatly enhances the gift of prophecy. Meaning the Tree allows you to see fate clearly. According to our legends, Emla inherited the prophetic gift from the Ash and passed it down to all her descendants. There is also a sign: if you put a sprig of the Ash under your pillow in the evening, you may have a prophetic dream.

The Ash's strength is so great that in the skies above Isa one can see rippling canvases of thousands and thousands of Threads of Fates. They become visible to everyone without exception, even to those who do not have any gift. It seems that these Threads are stretching straight from the crown of the Tree, and if you listen closely, you can discern a chorus of voices belonging to the owners of the Threads. We believe that this is a reflection of the Threads of everyone who has ever lived on Isa.

We do not know the exact history of the Ash, but we are convinced that it has a miraculous origin and serves as a bridge between worlds. From the darkness of centuries, a story is passed down - once our land was barren and empty - endless darkness dispersed only by fiery mountains among the icy deserts. And dragons reigned in this darkness. They were immortal and almost omnipotent.

But one day a ball of fire tore through the heavens. It fell on the earth and split it. And the dragons also fell, soaking that land with their blood. And he was born from that blood - Num, the creator of the living, and with him the First Spirits. But an island also rose from the melted waters, and the first of the Great Trees grew on the island. The Ash!

The Ash is a sentient being, our first ancestor. Our families of triplets are called "sprouts", like the sprouts of a tree, and our natural wanderlust is like the scattering of seeds the wind blows away from the parent tree.

Our beliefs were formed a long time ago, back in the days of the ancient Isa, and they have barely changed. They are based on belief in omens, signs.

Everything in the world is interconnected — everyone has their own Thread of the Path. And the Threads of the Path are intertwined, forming the Fabric of the World. Tracking the events taking place in the world, and signs of changes in the Pattern of Fate, one can predict the location of the threads in the next rows of the Fabric of the World.

Despite the uniqueness of each creature's Pattern of Fate, there are common elements of the Pattern that unambiguously indicate a specific scenario.

Since ancient times, in every large Gibberling village, there is a special house with a sacred loom in it. The Thread Keepers weave the great canvas on it - the Fabric of the World, and thereby determine the Patterns of Fate and try to direct the Threads of the Gibberling Path in a way that will form the most favorable pattern for us.

Thus, each generation of Gibberlings has its own "chronicle" - an endless carpet in which the fates of the entire tribe are entwined.

It should also be said that nothing prevents a clan or even an individual sprout from having their own signs and interpretation of certain patterns. Sometimes they diverge wildly, and the community has to hold a meeting to interpret conflicting signs or contact us, the Thread Keepers.

The Gibberlings learn to interpret signs all their lives from an early age. In Skalgard, no one would step out of the house if they spilled salt at breakfast. And if they see signs that Luck favors them, they would take on a seemingly impossible quest. It is said that some Gibberlings are born with great luck, which helps them get out of hopeless situations.

Those blessed with the gift of foresight are rather popular with their clan. Not everyone is allowed to disturb the Thread Keepers with their everyday issues, so it's often the seers that do readings for smaller matters. If, of course, it's a real seer, and not an enterprising fraud!

The loom is a real miracle. At the dawn of time, Ase himself carved it from the wood of the Prophetic Ash, and Emla etched sigils onto it, imbuing the loom with the great power to influence fate.

The yarn that is used for the threads is of great importance. For the Carpet of Fate, wool yarn is used, because it is filled with more vitality compared to plant-based yarn. Hair yarn has even more power and can have a huge impact on the owner. A thin and smooth thread promises an easy fate, while a rough and prickly one means a path full of trials. The color of the yarn chosen for babies will predict their personality. A knot accidentally tied on a thread is a serious disaster, and an accidental breakage of the thread promises a tragic premature death! Even the direction of the twisting of the thread matters: clockwise - for reflecting reality and divination, counterclockwise - for changing the already established fate.

Weaving of the Carpet of Fate is an unusual process. The Thread Keepers enter a prophetic trance. For weaving, we try to choose a particularly good time, when the border between the material and the mystical world becomes thinner, and the woven patterns acquire a truly fateful meaning. During such hours, simple spinners are forbidden to sew, weave and knit, so as not to accidentally create trouble for themselves, and even fishermen are strictly forbidden to make nets and tackle on their boats. If anyone disobeys, the item spun or woven at the time should be destroyed.
What do you want to know?

Who are you and what do you need from me? Your insolence is outrageous, young wanderer. I am busy - do you not see?

Wisdom lies in the contemplation of beauty as well.
Well, I must respect the guest's desire. What rune interests you?

The runes of the First? I will tell you everything.

There were many First ones. It would be impossible to count them all. Some long forgotten. Or never known. But the rune names... I will tell you about those. The ravens were Turaax, a friend to the Pridens, then Huginn and Muninn, friends to the Gibberlings. Kutkh was very cunning. There were many other First ones, soaring into the sky. Orn was an eagle, Roc - a rook, Vali - a falcon, Makchirgue - an owl.

And just as many of the First walked the earth. There were wolves among them. Akkya was a wolf. Stjorn was a panther; Heldig and Ekhe-Hoor were bears; Sakhyl - a fox; Jorm, Nidhogg and Haad were serpents; Kottr - a cat; Jofur - a boar; Hafur - a goat; Rhein and Roich were deer; Hvalur was a whale, Ratatoskr - a squirrel…

You wish to know about the runes of our heroes?

Among the Gibberlings, there were many heroes whose names the runes now bear. Ase and Emla are our ancestors. Wotin is a mighty leader, the father of Thorri, Lok, and Wald. Skaldr and Baldr are other heroes, skalds of ancient times; Freya and Iduna are the daughters of Emla; Wik, who built the first ships; Bers, who was a terrifying warrior; and even Seida who was a famous soothsayer. We remember and honor them all.

The sprouts were strong and hard to break. But there was also a black sheep in the herd. The family was split: one went into exile - the one who used to be a Thread Keeper. But she survived and came back, but what was broken could not be restored. Her descendants are all black. Seida and Unn are one of them.

There were runes that were rarely used. They were created in honor of the gods, monsters, and villains that people rarely mentioned. Among them was Kharyskhan, the leader of the Urun. Giants: Thrym, Aegir and Ymir; shifters: Garm, Hati, and Skoll. The werebear Bjorn; Alviss, the leader of the Zvergs; Ilco, the leader of the Heidruns; the guardian of the underground fire Surt; finally, Yol - the spirit of the year of change; Bolverk - the villain that betrayed the Gibberlings; Nagl - the dead wight; and Num himself, the creator of the living.

We have been to many places on Isa. Some of them are not even marked on the map.

There are interesting things there - creatures that no one has ever seen and various treasures. We collected a few things, but the headman said it's garbage. Still, someone would surely want to wear their great-grandfather's armor.

Maybe you'll buy it? We can sell it to you for Gibblers if you are interested.

There are almost no migratory birds left on Isa, except the seagulls circling over the Empty Sea. But there are still penguins out there. These birds do not fly, but swim well - almost like fish. They are funny to observe, so we breed them for entertainment. If you win the trust of Isa's Gibberlings, we can sell you one of them.

Squirrels have always been our friends, but ordinary squirrels on Isa are rather small. Our riding squirrels are quite a different matter, however. It's a special breed that lives on huge trees like our Great Ash. There are few of them left, and we cherish these creatures, so if you want to ride a squirrel, you must first win our trust. And have some of our coins, of course.

There are almost no migratory birds left on Isa, except the seagulls circling over the Empty Sea. But there are still penguins out there. These birds do not fly, but swim well - almost like fish. They are funny to observe, so we breed them for entertainment. If you win the trust of Isa's Gibberlings, we can sell you one of them.
Thank you so much! I heard... You help everyone...
Life is hard in our city... you'd do many things to get some bread...

quests: Good Deeds for the City: Questioning Students

t: Then it means I'm telling the truth, and Raskolnikov is lying! Well, how can you prove that I planted the money?
Let us suppose that's true. Then I lied to you, and Raskolnikov was telling the truth! What about the money?
And that means I told you the truth. And so did this floozy's mother, Ekaterina! And if I'm right, then who stole the money?
Then it means I lied to you, and Sonya's mother, Ekaterina, also lied or is confused about something... What are you getting at?
Then Ekaterina is right, but Sonya is lying! Lying without remorse! That's what I'm saying!
Then Sonya is telling the truth, but Ekaterina is lying... So? Let's say I did. What about the 90 rubles?
That would mean Amalia is right, but my treacherous friend Lebezin lied to you! I'm waiting for your conclusions.
Suppose I did. Then Lebezin was telling the truth, but Amalia lied to you! What, then? Can you draw the right conclusion?
Hahaha! That's what I was telling you! She stole the money! So Lebezin and Sonya are lying to you!
So you believe Lebezin and Sonya are telling the truth?
Ahaha! You seem to be confused! Come back once you figure out who is lying and who is telling the truth!

Yes, alas, I know this scoundrel! The thing is, he's my sister's fiancé. But that's in the past now! When he showed up here, I knew right away who he was and told him everything I thought of him. He's been nursing a grudge ever since. He's probably trying to get back at me.
I'm a simple student. I live here and study at the university nearby.
I didn't steal money from him! Yes, he offered me 10 rubles to help us out, but I didn't take the other 90! I didn't even touch it. It must have been planted!
It's no use. It looks like he's dead already.
Semyon Marmeladov seems to be crushed under the carriage.
It's the end of the world! Spiders! Spiders everywhere! Murderers!! Murderers!! The end is near... People!!
Murderers! Murderers! He stole from us and drank it all away! He ruined my life! And now he's dead! Murderers...
You can't help me... Sonya! Daughter! I'm sorry!
Ekaterina saw it and... lost it... There she is, wandering the streets...
This is horrible! He's dead... Oh, Tensess. What a nightmare...
Oh, I didn't see much... Just a silhouette... With a big axe...
It wasn't just arson! It's the dawn of a rebellion! Glory to Alice!

quests: Good Deeds for the City: Questioning Students

t: Long live the revolution! Soon we will overthrow the dark goddess!

quests: Good Deeds for the City: Questioning Students

t:
Alice? Verkhovensky?! Alarming news... I need to consider what to do next... I fear that my friend Rodion Raskolnikov might also be involved in this...

As for the murderer you're looking for, let Petrov check those who owed her... I can't think of anything else.
Oh, it's not arson. Probably just a prank... But they say a lot of things will burn down soon - police stations, palaces, and even churches... That's what Verkhovensky said...

Man is governed exclusively by the calculation of his own advantage. What we call sublime emotion or ideal aspiration-all that, in the general course of life, is completely insignificant in comparison with each person's pursuit of his own advantage.
Ah! Yes, I've heard about it... Some students recently received these... what are they called... components... That can be assembled into... what's it called... an incendiary device!
Soon we will strike again! Praise the Awakened!

quests: Good Deeds for the City: Questioning Students

t: Is this a conspiracy? It must have been a prank... But I hear a revolution is coming. My opinion? It's nonsense. This is hardly a revolution.
I heard something recently... Two students received these... what are they called... leaflets! And now they're scattered everywhere! Take a look for yourself. It's garbage, that's what!
Let us celebrate the emancipation of women!

Ahh! Damned obscurantists! They won't embrace gender equality! You hear "What should we do?" and "Who is to blame?", but I went and opened a sewing workshop and created a place for women where they could realize their full potential! And now I'm going to study medicine too!
You were all fooled... You believed it was easy to change the world...

It all started with the university... First Alice showed up and organized a club. She explained why her sister's rule was bad. Then this Verkhovensky came. He threatened everyone and bullied them into frankpledge, made them spy on each other...

Even those who initially had doubts were forced to take part in everything he planned... And those who refused mysteriously disappeared...
When I heard Iaver Bazar say we shouldn't recognize authorities, I felt so elated... as though I had seen the light!

Iaver Bazar opened my eyes! Down with authorities! I'm an old acquaintance of this great scholar. I owe him my rebirth... When I heard Iaver Bazar say we shouldn't recognize authorities, I felt so elated... as though I had seen the light! Down with authorities! Down with the Great Mages! Down with the gods!

It wasn't the money I needed, I needed something else...

I wrote an article for a newspaper some time ago...

An idea occurred to me: since ancient times, outstanding people have sacrificed the weak without hesitation! How many died during the Great Experiment? And how many people did Tep kill for the sake of his research? My idea was this: people, according to the law of nature, are divided into two categories: the bottom - the material that serves only to produce its own kind, and the worthy people who have a gift or talent...

These people are destroyers, those who destroy the present for greater good. In other words, outstanding people like Tep move the world forward. They are given more power than others, and they determine what is allowed and what is not.

Thus, villainy is permissible if the goal is good. The whole world is divided into people and nonentities.

I imagined that I, too, was a genius, a destroyer, and for some time I truly believed it. I needed to know as soon as possible whether I'm a nonentity or a person. Will I be able to cross a line? Am I brave enough to reach for something and take it? I'm a person...?

I came up with the theory, but I was not able to actually do it, to go for it... so that means I'm not who I thought I was.

Not what... Who!

Her name is... Aisa. Now she is here - in our world... The fates of the people she came across were changed, pulled out of the general pattern. Aisa can change my fate or yours.

But it's... meaningless. I still couldn't become what I wanted... I'm not a "person"...
Did I kill the old lady? I killed myself, not her!

After I confessed, Porfiry told me that my punishment will be keeping order on Jigran until I redeem myself. You'll benefit from this, too. Call me and I'll come - I'll serve my sentence and help improve your reputation with the townsfolk.
Thank you! I escaped from Aisa, but many could not. The Fateweavers still caught up with me. If it weren't for you...
I don't remember the way... I've been here for so long... The last thing I remember is falling from a height.

To be below or above is to be at the end or the beginning of the path of my fate.

If you see my fate, can you see my tracks, can you follow them from end to beginning?

Can you "fall upwards"?

Are you ready to hear me out? You won't like what I'm going to say...

Let's walk to the Cathedral...

As you can see, , Hiero came here with a whole army. His Paladins are quite resilient. While the Great Mages bowed before the Darkness, the Healers and Paladins rejected Hirkalla's rule. It was thanks to their faith that they managed to establish a foothold in this capital of shadows.

Now citizens come to this Temple - those who fear the Darkness. Our strength grows. Eventually we'll be able to challenge Hirkalla.

I believe in the Light, but there are many who have doubts. Look at them - they are scared and exhausted. That's how the Darkness finds its way into their hearts. When their Faith falters, the shield that's protecting the Temple gets weaker, too.

We shouldn't underestimate the Goddess of Darkness. She has a great force on her side, and many believed in her false resurrection, so we should be wary. But our caution shouldn't mean fear and dismay!

That's right, . Her eyes and ears are everywhere in the capitals of the League and Empire. You never know who succumbed to Darkness and who is still faithful to the Light. The temptation is too great, but believe me - I understand that Hirkalla is lying. Only a handful were resurrected. The rest turned into incorporeal shadows doomed to suffering. We, the Arisen, know what it's like. Most of us are bodiless Sparks, after all.

But there is good news as well. You managed to send a signal to Enod, and there has been a response. Three of the Children of Light, who had been observing Sarnaut for a long time, contacted Hiero and his warriors. Our task now is to hold our position until the forces from Enod arrive.

The main thing is to keep the barrier up. The Light from the Temple is spread using special beacons, but it's powered by our Faith. The stronger our Faith, the greater our power.

The Goddess of Darkness will spare no effort in her attempts to destroy this place. So we must keep our faith strong.
Our prayers have been answered! Look around you and believe.
Is there anything the power of Light can't do?

I represent Nefer Ur and Scientific Council here. We have our own view of Hirkalla and her pets. And Alice - I would love to speak with this elusive individual. By the way, do you have anything to say about this "Resurrection of Tep" that everyone is talking about? I just don't understand - I thought Klavdia had his Spark... How did Hirkalla get her hands on it? Or is that madman not actually Tep?

Oh, do you really want a lecture? You can ask the Healers about it.

Oh, well. I'll be brief.

Every living being, be it a human, elf, orc, animal, or even demon, has a Spark. No one knows what it actually is. You can call it a visible soul.

Free Sparks cannot linger too long in our world - they continually lose energy, fading over time.

In his time, Tep learned to extract it from Sparks. If you catch them, you can take what you need and use it for various purposes.

Your dark girlfriend released all Sparks from the storage that was similar to Tep's Pyramid.

That's why Jigran is full of free energy right now. Free for all.
A whole ocean of Darkness cannot extinguish a radiant Beacon of Light

My brothers came to Jigran before the dark goddess. The Elves of the House de Delice built this Cathedral to accustom vampire exiles to the Light.

But something else happened - Darkness swallowed the world, and it made its nest here. It wanted to chase away the Paladins, but they stood strong - and then Hirkalla threw her forces at them. But then a miracle occurred - her forces couldn't do anything. A strong shield of faith kept her dark creatures away from the Cathedral.

The number of brothers and sisters grew, and then they summoned me. Then...

You contacted Enod. Three observers came here: Ieziphael, Serahael, and Varadael. With them, our protection grew even stronger.

Then Alice came. I had no reason to trust her, but she explained that she wanted to fight against Hirkalla. I had no objections.

Their clash was... spectacular. The echo of their words resounded throughout the city - you can find it if you want.

Then Alice disappeared. And Hirkalla is sitting in her palace, dreaming of getting rid of us.
I think everyone should learn to love life more than anything else.

Most of them exist on the verge of transforming into a silent Spark - they don't have enough energy to act without an ether body. They need energy not to become Sparks. You can either take it from other, weaker entities, or someone powerful can grant it to you.

Unfortunately, most decided to harvest Sparks of the other awakened. Those people are called owners of dead souls, and some even sell them.

There are also the distorted creatures of Darkness and mindless ghosts. They are nothing but predators who steal our energy.
Where can I get a new coat? I don't even have money...
My friend, information is valuable. If you do me a favor, I will tell you everything I know.
Falling in love does not mean loving. You can fall in love even if you hate them!
Eh, yes, I would be glad to help, but I have a problem... If you can handle it, I'll tell you everything!
My throat is so dry I don't feel like talking. If you help me with that, I'll tell you everything.
Uhh, why are you here, buddy? Would you like to try some kebab? Good kebab. Fresh!
Who is Selifan? Do you mean Ivan? I don't remember him, hah! But you know what? If you bring me ten Sparks, it will refresh my memory!
Well, buddy! For you and Selifan, I'll spare nothing. If you're planning a boozy evening, don't forget Zlatan!
Do you take me for a fool?
Come on, you think I don't understand? The good of the empress is above all!
What? How dare you?! This is an insult!

quests: Dark Cunning: Search for the Agent

t: Greetings! My colleagues and I decided to go to the circus...

quests: Dark Cunning: Search for the Agent

t: Excellent, we'll settle the rest later...
It's a strange feeling - to be alive again.

Well, the ghosts are those who died and then came back to life.

They lived in the Old Era. Performed different deeds, both heroic and mundane.

But everything changed for some of the people I knew. They were famous, they were an important part of history. But now...

They are odd people out. Unwanted. Discarded.

I... don't understand who could have done that. I might be the only one remembering the old version of the story.

Understand who interfered with history.

I doubt that it was Nihaz or Hirkalla - I would have known if it was them.

It can't be Cosmos - right now his ability to manipulate the Observatory is very limited.

Someone else is operating on a different level. You and I must find them. I suggest you ask my sister and her minions. They have to know something... I hope you don't mind becoming a spy?

Oh please, no need for all that, . For some odd reason she seems to favor you, so you're the perfect candidate for infiltrating her ranks.

You'll have to play along for a bit.

Do what she says. Kill if she tells you to. Lie if she tells you to. Don't worry about getting your hands dirty. We need to save Sarnaut! By any means necessary!

Hey, hey, just don't get carried away, . You are a spy, not her loyal servant...

Your task is to worm yourself into Hirkalla's confidence. She seems to favor you for some odd reason. Pretend to follow her orders, no matter what she asks of you. And at the right moment... you'll betray her. For the good of Sarnaut!
What a strange thing to hear! Is there a force that can change someone's destiny? Alice told me you had certain abilities. That you are a Weaver! Perhaps you'll tell me about your adventures?

Yes, I believe the awakened can do without our help for now. We have dealt with the worst trouble for now - Tep.

We need to find out who has stolen peoples' destinies! I'm sure we'll find an answer to this question in Hirkalla's palace. Her generals receive reports from all over the allod. If anything strange has happened, they'll know of it.
I can't believe it. I run my hands over my body but still can't get used to it.
I wish it would all start soon!
You can't love what you don't know!
Our lovers of freedom are first and foremost lackeys and only seek to clean someone's boots.
